method: Production renderer, models and per-step simulation (Game.update's wildlife steps, the calendar held so no day redraw lands mid-shot) in headless Chrome on the GPU, at a fixed 30 fps timestep. Scenes are seeded restored maps (release-fixtures, Math.random seeded) with posed animals that then behave on their own; keystone clips start from production moment triggers (website-moment-fixtures). Encoded in the page with WebCodecs (H.264 High, VP9), muxed by tools/video-mux.mjs. Crossfade loops dissolve the last second into the first; a dissolve joins the overhead view to eye level. Nothing is generated or painted.

clips.title: Hollis creek flyover
clips.description: A steady drift up the restored Hollis creek at golden hour, at watch pace: Roosevelt elk, a black-tailed deer, a beaver, a great blue heron and wood ducks posed at the water, then left to their own behaviour.

clips.title: Hollis creek flyover
clips.description: A steady drift up the restored Hollis creek at golden hour, at watch pace: Roosevelt elk, a black-tailed deer, a beaver, a great blue heron and wood ducks posed at the water, then left to their own behaviour.

clips.title: From the map to the forest floor
clips.description: The overhead view of restored Hollis pushes in on a Roosevelt elk at the creek, then dissolves to eye level behind it as it walks up the bank (sent there through the game's pathfinding). Both are the game's own cameras (the usual view, then watch mode's eye level).

clips.title: Keystone moment: the elk rut
clips.description: Two adult Roosevelt elk during the antler-contact beat of the autumn rut. The bout is initialized through the production social behavior. The camera turns steadily round them while the bout plays out at watch pace.

clips.title: Lions stalk wildebeest
clips.description: Two hungry lions posed downwind of a grazing wildebeest herd on restored grassland; the hunt is begun through the game's own startHunt and the stalk, rush and outcome are the simulation's.

clips.title: Vultures circle down to a kill
clips.description: A pride's fresh buffalo kill (the catch staged through the game's own catch path) with hungry vultures soaring nearby; they find the carcass and spiral down to it by the game's scavenging behaviour.

clips.title: A blacktip shark chases longtom
clips.description: A hungry blacktip reef shark posed a few tiles from a school of longtom over the reef; the hunt is begun through the game's own startHunt, and the chase, the longtom's skipping escape across the surface and the outcome are the simulation's.

clips.title: An anaconda strikes from the water
clips.description: A hungry green anaconda posed in the lake shallows and two thirsty capybara posed up the bank (run seed 12). The capybara come down to drink, and the snake's own lie-in-wait behaviour picks one, strikes and feeds; nothing after the posing is scripted.

clips.title: A harpy eagle takes a howler monkey
clips.description: A hungry harpy eagle posed on a crown near a howler troop in restored forest; the hunt is begun through the game's own startHunt, and the drop from the perch, the catch roll and carrying the catch off are the simulation's.

clips.title: A red-tailed hawk takes a chipmunk
clips.description: A hungry red-tailed hawk posed on the wing over backyards near two foraging chipmunks (run seed 1); the hunt is begun through the game's own startHunt, and the circling, the stoop, the catch roll and carrying the catch to a perch are the simulation's.

clips.title: A tiger stalks sambar
clips.description: A hungry tiger posed at the forest edge near three grazing sambar deer; the hunt is begun through the game's own startHunt, and the stalk, rush and outcome are the simulation's.

clips.title: Keystone moment: hatchlings run for the sea
clips.description: Olive ridley hatchlings at the beach edge. The map’s production nest-hatching event creates the juveniles and their route toward the sea; nest positions and age are staged. The camera follows them down the beach at watch pace.
